title: Bayesian Intelligence from the Outside
abstract: arXiv:2609.14724v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Inferring intelligence from observable behavior is a foundational challenge in artificial intelligence. We develop a theory of Bayesian intelligence for agents such as language models. Each prompt induces a possibly imperfect internal experiment; the agent updates a full-support prior by Bayes' rule and faithfully reports its posterior over the possible answers to the question. Repetitions draw fresh, independent outcomes from the same unobserved experiment at one fixed state. We show that the agent's behavior admits this explanation if and only if its reports are not fully contradictory, i.e., some state remains possible under every report across all prompts. Report frequencies and the sizes of positive probabilities impose no further restrictions. We further propose and characterize the behavioral implications of an intelligence order that makes the behavior of two agents consistent with one agent having access to a more informative ex

translated_title: 外部视角下的贝叶斯智能
translated_abstract: 从可观察行为中推断智能是人工智能领域的一个基础性挑战。我们为语言模型等智能体发展了一套贝叶斯智能理论。每个提示词会引发一个可能不完美的内部实验；智能体通过贝叶斯法则更新一个全支撑先验，并忠实地报告其对问题各种可能答案的后验分布。重复提问会在同一固定状态下从同一未观察到的实验中抽取全新的独立结果。我们证明，当且仅当智能体的报告并非完全自相矛盾时——即在所有提示下的每次报告中始终存在某个仍然可能的状态——其行为才符合这种贝叶斯解释。报告的频率以及正概率的大小不再构成进一步的限制。我们进一步提出并刻画了一种智能序的行为含义，该智能序使得两个智能体的行为与其中一个智能体能够获取更具信息量的实验相一致。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种从外部可观察行为推断语言模型等智能体智能的贝叶斯理论，证明了当且仅当智能体的报告不完全自相矛盾时其行为才能被贝叶斯更新解释，并提出了一种刻画智能体间信息优势的智能序。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a Bayesian theory of intelligence for agents such as language models, showing that an agent's behavior admits a Bayesian explanation if and only if its reports are not fully contradictory, and proposes an intelligence order that characterizes when one agent has access to a more informative experiment.
